subject: Human Body
title: The Esophagus Highway
description: A quick win: understand The Esophagus Highway.

hook.text: Food doesn't fall to your stomach by gravity. Muscles push it there even if you eat upside down.

buildup.text: The esophagus is a 25 cm muscular tube connecting the throat to the stomach. It has no digestive role itself.

discovery.text: Peristalsis: wave-like muscle contractions squeeze food downward. It takes 6–8 seconds to reach the stomach.

twist.text: Astronauts eat normally in space because peristalsis works without gravity. The muscles do all the work.

climax.text: The esophagus is a one-way delivery pipe. Peristalsis keeps food moving in the right direction reliably.

punchline.text: Gravity helps, but your muscles do the real work.

quiz.question: What moves food through the esophagus?
